title: UK public sector finances, September 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — not the Budget's input but the first out-of-sample check on it, and it shares its minute with UK CPI
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/publicsectorfinancesukseptember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the publisher's own release-calendar entry reads verbatim 'Public sector finances, UK: September 2026', '21 October 2026 at 7:00am', describing the headline measures 'net borrowing net cash requirement and net debt', and marked 'This release is not yet published.' The 07:00 collision with uk-cpi-2026-10-21 is independently primary: ons.gov.uk/releases/consumerpriceinflationukseptember2026, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200), reads 'Consumer price inflation, UK: September 2026', '21 October 2026 7:00am', also not yet published — two publisher pages, one minute. Corroborated by publication-cadence arithmetic on the ONS's own past-release listing (70 PSF bulletins, 2020-11-20 to 2026-08-21, every one on the 19th-26th of the month). The statutory gov.uk pre-announcement register could not be reached for this release (404 on the expected slug, 2026-09-09) and is NOT claimed as a source. Filed estimate on two counts this lane records for every ONS entry: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a foreign national statistics institute, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep. Canonical file written 2026-09-09 from proposals/uk-public-sector-finances-2026-10-21.from-uk-labour-market-2026-10-20.json
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-labour-market-2026-10-20 LANE 2026-09-09; CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY ITS OWN never-assessed RESEARCH THE SAME DAY, WHICH CORRECTED THE PREMISE IT WAS FILED UNDER. The proposal justified the slot as 'the number against which the Chancellor's headroom arithmetic is scored seven days later' at the 2026-10-28 Budget. Measured against the OBR's own two most recent published forecast timetables, that is calendar-true and forecast-false: the November 2025 EFO's final pre-measures FISCAL forecast took its determinants over the ten working days to 2025-10-21 — 36 days before the 2025-11-26 Budget — with only measures-driven stages completed after (2025-11-21); the October 2024 EFO's pre-measures forecast was finalised 2024-09-26, 34 days before the 2024-10-30 Budget, so the 2024-10-22 September borrowing print (D-8, the exact analogue of this one at D-7) missed it. Both search-relayed — obr.uk 403s this lane. The honest restatement, which is this entry's title: the print inside the Budget's forecast is the 2026-09-22 one (August data, proposed in the same PR); THIS print is the first public borrowing number that can CONTRADICT the EFO, published seven days before it, and the ONS bulletin's own 'versus forecast' line will still be scored against the March 2026 EFO (ons.gov.uk July 2026 bulletin, fetched 2026-09-09) — a profile replaced a week later. Live baseline it lands on: borrowing in the financial year to July 2026 £56.7bn, £6.0bn (9.6%) below last year but £2.3bn ABOVE the OBR March 2026 forecast; debt 94.1% of GDP. Tiered LOW and the tier is measured, not inherited: across 70 PSF release days since 2020-11-20 the UK gilt ETF IGLT.L moved 1.14x an ordinary day (t = 1.02), GBP/USD 0.88x, the US 10y 0.90x, the FTSE 100 0.92x — four nulls. symbols: [], no house playbook is fiscal-, rates- or sterling-keyed, and this repo tracks no UK-listed name. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
